chapter: Nola band, day job and nightclub work
title: Working hard on trumpet around a day job; the San Souci dance hall
summary: He practiced evenings after day work, and the band played three nights a week at San Souci on Howard Street.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah. Then you went with Dr. Robert.

Yeah, I worked pretty hard on the instrument. See, it might sound like I was making plenty of headway to you, but I was working like a dog to do it too. I was working day, I had a day job, and I was trying to do both, and I had to concentrate plenty on the trumpet, you know, in evenings from work, and all times I had on.
How often did the Supreme Band play? Did you play every night or?
Well no, I'll tell you, one time we played three nights a week. You know, dance hall, I think the name of the dance hall was, San Suci. Uh huh. Played three nights a week, yeah.
That was on, uh, on Howard, I would say between Washington and 6th.

They used to have, I think, I've seen the letters in the sidewalk, or something, somebody pointed it out to me up there. I forget who it was, years ago. Yeah? Because I know where the place was, it's right there on Highway.
Yeah, on Highway between 6th and Washington. Yeah, I understand.
